Since the evidence contains the definition of M as a binary tool mask and shows its integral use in the framework described, the facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.

The source explicitly defines the binocular depth loss as $L_{depth}^B$ and the monocular depth loss as $L_{depth}^M$. In the final objective function equation (8), the term is written as $L_{depth}^{-1} / L_{depth}^{-1}$. The notes clarify that the binocular loss uses reciprocal depth ($D^{-1}$) and the monocular loss uses correlation. The notation in the claim ($L_{depth}^{-1} / L_{depth}^{-1}$) appears to be a transcription artifact or specific notation in the source text representing the combination of these two terms (Binocular and Monocular), which is confirmed by the text stating the depth rendering constraint consists of $L_{depth}^B / L_{depth}^M$ for binocular/monocular input. The claim correctly identifies that this part of the equation denotes the combined binocular and monocular depth loss terms.
